overview: The task used two existing lab servers to explore a shared web-service address. I labeled the IIS content on each node so captures of the cluster URL could identify which server responded.
environment: Distinct Node A and Node B web-page labels

steps.title: Prepare the web roles and NLB features
steps.description: I reused the existing lab VMs to conserve resources. The notes record IIS already present on DC01 and IIS plus NLB installation on DC02.

steps.title: Give the node pages distinct labels
steps.description: I changed the IIS page artwork to identify NLB NODE A and NLB NODE B, providing a visible indication of the responding host.

steps.title: Configure the shared cluster address
steps.description: I configured the NLB virtual address, node identities and priorities using the lab’s unicast configuration.

steps.title: Check cluster convergence
steps.description: I inspected Network Load Balancing Manager. The captured list shows both nodes Converged with distinct dedicated addresses and priorities.

steps.title: Capture the shared URL responding from Node A
steps.description: I opened the cluster address and recorded the IIS page labeled NLB NODE A.

steps.title: Capture the shared URL responding from Node B
steps.description: I also retained the same cluster address displaying NLB NODE B, showing that the other node could serve that address.

checks.title: Cluster convergence
checks.description: Both nodes are shown as Converged in the cluster management view.

checks.title: Responses from both node identities
checks.description: The cluster URL is captured displaying each node’s distinct IIS label.

lessons: A shared virtual address and a node’s dedicated address serve different purposes.
Visible node labels help identify the host serving a request.
Two node responses do not quantify balanced traffic, recovery time or an outage test.
NLB handles traffic distribution differently from stateful failover clustering and shared-storage recovery.
scope: The evidence shows convergence and responses from two node identities. It does not document a controlled failure, recovery-time measurement, application health check or evenly distributed load. Reusing domain-controller VMs was a resource-constrained lab choice.
